label: Acts 8:1
text: Saul was consenting to his death. A great persecution arose against the assembly which was in Jerusalem in that day. They were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except for the apostles.

label: Acts 8:2
text: Devout men buried Stephen, and lamented greatly over him.

label: Acts 8:3
text: But Saul ravaged the assembly, entering into every house, and dragged both men and women off to prison.

label: Acts 8:4
text: Therefore those who were scattered abroad went around preaching the word.

label: Acts 8:5
text: Philip went down to the city of Samaria, and proclaimed to them the Christ.

label: Acts 8:6
text: The multitudes listened with one accord to the things that were spoken by Philip, when they heard and saw the signs which he did.

label: Acts 8:7
text: For unclean spirits came out of many of those who had them. They came out, crying with a loud voice. Many who had been paralyzed and lame were healed.

label: Acts 8:8
text: There was great joy in that city.

label: Acts 8:9
text: But there was a certain man, Simon by name, who used to practice sorcery in the city, and amazed the people of Samaria, making himself out to be some great one,

label: Acts 8:10
text: to whom they all listened, from the least to the greatest, saying, “This man is that great power of God.”

label: Acts 8:11
text: They listened to him, because for a long time he had amazed them with his sorceries.

label: Acts 8:12
text: But when they believed Philip preaching good news concerning God’s Kingdom and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

label: Acts 8:13
text: Simon himself also believed. Being baptized, he continued with Philip. Seeing signs and great miracles occurring, he was amazed.

label: Acts 8:14
text: Now when the apostles who were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them,

label: Acts 8:15
text: who, when they had come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Spirit;

label: Acts 8:16
text: for as yet he had fallen on none of them. They had only been baptized in the name of Christ Jesus.

label: Acts 8:17
text: Then they laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.

label: Acts 8:18
text: Now when Simon saw that the Holy Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered them money,

label: Acts 8:19
text: saying, “Give me also this power, that whomever I lay my hands on may receive the Holy Spirit.”

label: Acts 8:20
text: But Peter said to him, “May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money!

label: Acts 8:21
text: You have neither part nor lot in this matter, for your heart isn’t right before God.

label: Acts 8:22
text: Repent therefore of this, your wickedness, and ask God if perhaps the thought of your heart may be forgiven you.

label: Acts 8:23
text: For I see that you are in the poison of bitterness and in the bondage of iniquity.”

label: Acts 8:24
text: Simon answered, “Pray for me to the Lord, that none of the things which you have spoken happen to me.”

label: Acts 8:25
text: They therefore, when they had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, and preached the Good News to many villages of the Samaritans.

label: Acts 8:26
text: But an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, “Arise, and go toward the south to the way that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza. This is a desert.”

variants.reading: kata mesembrian read as 'at noon' rather than 'toward the south'
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Acts 8' article: the Greek may mean 'towards the south' or 'at noon'; a marginal note in the Revised Version, the text of the Jerusalem Bible and the Ethiopic text state 'at noon'. No manuscript node of this graph carries the reading.

label: Acts 8:27
text: He arose and went; and behold, there was a man of Ethiopia, a eunuch of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasure, who had come to Jerusalem to worship.

label: Acts 8:28
text: He was returning and sitting in his chariot, and was reading the prophet Isaiah.

label: Acts 8:29
text: The Spirit said to Philip, “Go near, and join yourself to this chariot.”

label: Acts 8:30
text: Philip ran to him, and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet, and said, “Do you understand what you are reading?”

label: Acts 8:31
text: He said, “How can I, unless someone explains it to me?” He begged Philip to come up and sit with him.

label: Acts 8:32
text:
Now the passage of the Scripture which he was reading was this,
“He was led as a sheep to the slaughter.
As a lamb before his shearer is silent,
so he doesn’t open his mouth.

label: Acts 8:33
text:
In his humiliation, his judgment was taken away.
Who will declare His generation?
For his life is taken from the earth.”

label: Acts 8:34
text: The eunuch answered Philip, “Who is the prophet talking about? About himself, or about someone else?”

label: Acts 8:35
text: Philip opened his mouth, and beginning from this Scripture, preached to him about Jesus.

label: Acts 8:36
text: As they went on the way, they came to some water, and the eunuch said, “Behold, here is water. What is keeping me from being baptized?”

variants.reading: KJV: 'And Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.' Verse omitted in most modern versions
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles' article: 'verse omitted by P45, P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, C, P, Psi, 049...' — Sinaiticus and Vaticanus both omit it; the omission carries UBS confidence A; cited by Irenaeus (c. 180) and present in the Old Latin and Vulgate. No preserves edge from either codex is written for this verse.

label: Acts 8:38
text: He commanded the chariot to stand still, and they both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.

label: Acts 8:39
text: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away, and the eunuch didn’t see him any more, for he went on his way rejoicing.

variants.reading: 'the Holy Spirit fell on the eunuch, and an angel of the Lord caught up Philip'
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles' article lists this reading for A, 36a, 94, 103, 307, 322, 323, 385, 453, 467, 945, 1739, it, vg, syr-h; none of these witnesses is a manuscript node of this graph.

label: Acts 8:40
text: But Philip was found at Azotus. Passing through, he preached the Good News to all the cities, until he came to Caesarea.

label: The Ethiopian eunuch (treasurer of the Kandake)
note: Unnamed in Acts 8:27; the Kandake page of the Ethiopian Orthodox tradition names him Bachos (via Irenaeus 'Simeon Bachos').

label: The Kandake of Kush ('Candace, queen of the Ethiopians')
note: Candace is a title (Meroitic kdke) for a queen or queen mother of Kush, treated by Greek and Roman writers as a name. The specific queen of Acts 8:27 is unnamed; Strabo's Candace (c. 25 BCE) is usually identified as Amanirenas.

periods: Israelite capital; Hellenistic; refounded as Sebaste by Herod the Great (late 1st century BC); Roman; Byzantine

label: Caesarea Maritima (Herod's port city, excavated)
excavators: excavated in the 1950s and 1960s for archaeological purposes (fetched Wikipedia article names no director)

label: The Jerusalem persecution; all scattered through Judea and Samaria except the apostles
statement: A great persecution arose against the assembly which was in Jerusalem, and all were scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except for the apostles.

label: Devout men buried Stephen and lamented over him
statement: Devout men buried Stephen and lamented greatly over him.

label: Saul ravaged the assembly, dragging men and women to prison
statement: Saul ravaged the assembly, entering into every house, and dragged both men and women off to prison.

label: Philip went down to the city of Samaria and proclaimed the Christ
statement: Philip went down to the city of Samaria, and proclaimed to them the Christ.

label: The 'city of Samaria' is Herod's Sebaste
statement: The 'city of Samaria' Philip visited was the old Israelite capital, refounded and renamed Sebaste by Herod the Great in honour of Augustus.

label: Unclean spirits expelled; many paralyzed and lame healed
statement: Unclean spirits came out of many of those who had them, crying with a loud voice, and many who had been paralyzed and lame were healed.
note: Miracle claim: searched honestly, recorded none-found. Setting evidence sits on the Samaria claims, not on the miracle.

label: Simon the sorcerer amazed the people of Samaria
statement: A man named Simon practised sorcery in the city and amazed the people of Samaria, who called him 'that great power of God'.

label: Samaritans believed Philip and were baptized
statement: When the Samaritans believed Philip preaching good news concerning God's Kingdom and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

label: Simon himself believed and was baptized
statement: Simon himself also believed; being baptized, he continued with Philip, amazed at the signs and great miracles.

label: The apostles sent Peter and John to Samaria
statement: When the apostles who were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.

label: The Spirit given through the laying on of the apostles' hands
statement: The Samaritan believers, baptized in the name of Christ Jesus, received the Holy Spirit only when Peter and John laid their hands on them.

label: Simon offered money for the power of the Spirit ('simony')
statement: Simon offered the apostles money for the power to give the Holy Spirit through the laying on of his hands, and Peter rebuked him: 'May your silver perish with you.'

label: The gospel preached in many villages of the Samaritans
statement: Peter and John, returning to Jerusalem, testified and preached the good news to many villages of the Samaritans.

label: The desert road from Jerusalem to Gaza
statement: There was a road going down from Jerusalem to Gaza, and the way was desert.

label: 'Candace' is the Kandake title of the queens of Kush
statement: 'Candace' is the title (Meroitic kdke) of a queen or queen mother of the kingdom of Kush, which Greek and Roman writers treated as a personal name; it is not the name of one queen.

label: The Ethiopian eunuch, a court official over all the Kandake's treasure
statement: The Ethiopian eunuch was a court official of great authority under the Kandake, in charge of all her treasure.

label: The eunuch had come to Jerusalem to worship
statement: The Ethiopian eunuch had come to Jerusalem to worship.

label: The eunuch read the prophet Isaiah in his chariot
statement: The eunuch was returning home, sitting in his chariot, and was reading the prophet Isaiah.

label: The passage read was Isaiah 53:7-8
statement: The passage of Scripture the eunuch was reading was Isaiah 53:7-8 ('He was led as a sheep to the slaughter... for his life is taken from the earth').

label: Philip baptized the eunuch at water on the road
statement: When they came to some water on the way, the eunuch asked for baptism, and Philip baptized him.

label: The Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away
statement: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more, and went on his way rejoicing.
note: Miracle claim: searched honestly, recorded none-found.

label: Philip found at Azotus, preaching until Caesarea
statement: Philip was found at Azotus, and passing through, preached the good news in all the cities until he came to Caesarea.
